In [[classical mechanics]], a '''vague torus''' is a region in [[phase space]] that is characterized by approximate [[constants of motion]], as opposed to an actual torus defined by exact constants of motion.
The concept of vague tori is used to describe regular ([[Quasiperiodic motion|quasiperiodic]]) segments of otherwise [[chaos theory|chaotic]] trajectories.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Dana | first1 = I. | title = Type specification of chaos | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.2387 | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 70 | issue = 16 | pages = 2387–2390 | year = 1993 | pmid =  10053549|bibcode = 1993PhRvL..70.2387D }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Reinhardt | first1 = W. P. | title = Chaotic dynamics, semiclassical quantization, and mode-mode energy transfer: The Boulder view | doi = 10.1021/j100209a008 | journal = The Journal of Physical Chemistry | volume = 86 | issue = 12 | pages = 2158–2165 | year = 1982 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Shirts | first1 = R. B. | title = Approximate constants of motion for classically chaotic vibrational dynamics: Vague tori, semiclassical quantization, and classical intramolecular energy flow | doi = 10.1063/1.443697 | journal = The Journal of Chemical Physics | volume = 77 | issue = 10 | pages = 5204–5217 | year = 1982 |bibcode = 1982JChPh..77.5204S }}</ref>
